rules.rule: Masculine consonant stems43: singular zero/es/e/zero; plural as/a/um/as. Do not infer gender or class merely from an English translation.

Syncope43.4 requires a heavy initial and light second syllable in the stated model; compare ēðel→ēðles with hęngest retaining e. Noun classes and explicitly listed exceptions outrank a mechanical spelling rule.

Neuter47 nominative/accusative plural takes u for the stated short monosyllabic model, zero for the heavy model. Disyllables and compounds need their own diagnostic statement rather than automatic assignment from a final spelling. Cook47.1 explicitly lists mægnu in nominative/accusative plural; the selected table retains mægen- in all oblique forms. Final long vowels/diphthongs and consonant clusters matter, including palmtwīg and nest.
Feminine51.5 -nes/-en/-el/-et doubles the final consonant in oblique forms and retains e. Explicit examples and glossary assignments govern cnēoris and ðīnen.
Weak53 m-a/f-e: oblique singular an, plural an/ena/um/an. Weak neuter ēare keeps e in nominative/accusative singular and has genitive plural ēarna.
Strong/weak adjective choice is a syntactic choice. Substantival use is separately identified; familiar adjective forms do not automatically teach a new lexical meaning or new participial government.

Tables are complete only within their named number/sense and case scope. Singular-only teaching is an assignment boundary, never an assertion that the word is defective. Supplied source forms must be visible at the task and cannot be independent-recall targets.

Direct-address adjectives take weak forms under Cook55 and prior u09-vocative-weak-adjective. Thus the selected address forms are wæstmbǣran, gefiðredan, geongan and ealdan. Eall has its separately taught quantifier pattern; its presence does not make every neighboring modifier strong.
